simple.meaning: נְטִישָׁה (nᵉṭîyshâh) is a Hebrew animal word meaning “a tendril (as an offshoot).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Isaiah 18:5. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to נְטִישָׁה (H5189) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.full: H5189. netishah [ נְטִישָׁה ] noun feminine twig, tendril of vine (as spreading , compare √ Niph`al 3 ); — only plural הֵתַז הֵסִיר הַנְּטִישׁוֺת Isa 18:5 the tendrils he hath removed , compare נְטִישׁוֺתֶיהָ הָסִירוּ Jer 5:10 (apparently cited from Isaiah; explanation by Finn Journ. Trans. Vict. Inst. xxii. 306 f. from use by shepherds of poterium spinosum , called nettsh , as defence of sheepfolds), — in both of destroying city (under figure of vineyard); יָם עָ֑בְרוּ נְטִישֹׁתַיִךְ 48:32 thy tendrils went over the sea (figurative of prosperity of Moab). [ נִי ] see נהה .

occurrences.englishText: For before the harvest, when the blossom is over, and the flower becomes a ripening grape, he will cut off the sprigs with pruning hooks, and he will cut down and take away the spreading branches.
“Go up on her walls, and destroy; but don’t make a full end. Take away her branches, for they are not Yahweh’s.
With more than the weeping of Jazer
